# Test-ZbxConfiguration

## SYNOPSIS

Checks a configuration document before it is imported.

## SYNTAX

### Path (Default)

```
Test-ZbxConfiguration [-Path] <string[]> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] [-Quiet] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Text

```
Test-ZbxConfiguration -Source <string> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] [-Quiet] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### LiteralPath

```
Test-ZbxConfiguration -LiteralPath <string[]> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] [-Quiet] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Test-ZbxConfiguration cmdlet reads a configuration document (text, or files with -Path, which takes wildcards, or -LiteralPath) in JSON, XML or YAML, the format told from its first character or given with -Format, and reports whether it is well formed and which plaintext secrets, such as passwords or PSKs, it carries. It runs on the client and sends nothing to a server. -Quiet writes only $true or $false, for a script's if.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Check an exported document for secrets

```powershell
Export-ZbxConfiguration -Host 'web-01' | Test-ZbxConfiguration
```

Export-ZbxConfiguration redacts secrets by default; the report lists any that are still there.

### Example 2: Check that a document is well formed before importing it

```powershell
'{"zabbix_export":{"version":"7.0","host_groups":[{"uuid":"a571c0d144b14fd4a87a9d9b2aa9fcd6","name":"Linux servers"}]}}' | Test-ZbxConfiguration -Quiet
'{"zabbix_export":' | Test-ZbxConfiguration -Quiet
```

-Quiet writes $true or $false; the second document is cut off, so it is not well formed.
